match.reason: The bank card teaches exactly the brief's idea, that a catalyst gives a path with lower activation energy and is not used up, at an introductory depth that suits Unit 3 and both questions are fair for a VCE student.

confirm.reason: The bank point teaches activation energy and catalysts together, so it is broader than this catalyst-only point, and the course likely covers activation energy in its own point.

draft.title: Catalysts
card: Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles need to react. A catalyst is a substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up.
A catalyst gives the reaction a different path with a lower activation energy. More collisions then have enough energy to react, so the rate rises.
The catalyst takes part in the reaction but is regenerated by the end. It is the same amount and chemical form afterwards, so a small amount can be used again and again.
A catalyst does not change the energy of the reactants or products, so it does not change the overall energy released or absorbed.
draft.remember: A catalyst lowers activation energy by a new path and is not used up.

a.q: What change inside a reaction explains why adding a catalyst increases the rate?
opts: A different path needs less activation energy
Colliding particles carry more energy than before
The reactants start at a higher energy
Some of the catalyst turns into extra product
a.why: The new path needs less energy, so a larger share of collisions succeed. Giving colliding particles more energy describes heating, not a catalyst, which leaves the energy of the particles unchanged.
a.clue: The catalyst changes the path, not the particles.

b.q: Priya adds manganese dioxide to hydrogen peroxide and oxygen bubbles off faster. She filters out the solid afterwards. What would she find?
opts: The same mass of manganese dioxide as she added
Less manganese dioxide, as it was used up
More manganese dioxide, as it formed from the reaction
The same mass, but it has become a different compound
b.why: A catalyst is regenerated, so the same amount remains in the same chemical form. Less remaining would mean it was consumed, which a catalyst is not.
b.clue: Does a catalyst get used up or changed by the end?

a.best: A different path needs less activation energy

b.best: The same mass of manganese dioxide as she added
